explained.headline: Israel Faces Coalition Gridlock After General Election

happened.text: Partial results from Israel's general election showed that Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's Likud-led bloc held a lead with 53 seats, while the opposition bloc led by Gadi Eisenkot stood at 48 seats in the 120-seat Knesset.

Both major blocs fell short of the 61 seats required to form a secure majority, leaving the parliament deadlocked as nearly half a million absentee and double-envelope ballots awaited full tabulation.

background.text: Gadi Eisenkot is a retired general and former military commander who leads the centrist Yashar party and heads the anti-Netanyahu opposition alliance.
Between April 2019 and November 2022, Israel held five general elections in rapid succession due to recurring difficulties in forming stable governing coalitions.

matters.text: Experts cited by the sources indicate that a new Israeli government is unlikely to alter policies regarding Palestinian statehood or military operations in neighbouring countries.
United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Türk stated his hope that the incoming administration would alter its approach to international law and military conduct.
President Isaac Herzog urged political leaders to approach coalition negotiations with an open mind to prevent the country from being forced into another round of elections.

uncertain.text: The final distribution of seats remained subject to change pending the complete counting of hundreds of thousands of absentee double-envelope ballots cast by soldiers, diplomats and prisoners.
It remained unclear which political figure President Isaac Herzog would ultimately task with forming a government once official results are finalized.
The sources report that coalition talks face uncertainty because Jewish opposition parties remain divided over whether to negotiate with Arab-majority parties to secure a majority.

terms.definition: The unicameral national legislature of Israel.
An absentee voting method used by military personnel, diplomats, prisoners and others unable to visit their assigned polling stations.

removed.text: Arab-majority parties achieved a record result, winning between 17 and 19 seats following a surge in voter turnout.

Benjamin Netanyahu is Israel's longest-serving prime minister, and the election took place amid ongoing regional conflicts involving Gaza, Lebanon, Syria and Iran following the 7 October 2023 attacks by Hamas.
why: Evidence mentions conflict with Syria but does not support the claim Netanyahu is the longest-serving PM.

explained.headline: African leaders gather in Moscow for summit as Russia deepens ties

happened.text: African leaders and government delegations are gathering in Moscow for the Russia-Africa Summit.
The Kremlin expects delegations from 48 countries, including 22 heads of state, to attend the meetings.
The Kremlin aims to demonstrate its continued political relevance despite international pressure.

background.text: In 2019, 43 African heads of state or government attended the inaugural summit in Sochi, Russia.
Following the invasion of Ukraine, only 17 heads of state attended the second summit held in St Petersburg in 2023.
Moscow has expanded its security footprint in the Sahel through Africa Corps, which is controlled by Russia’s Ministry of Defence and replaced the Wagner Group.

matters.text: Beverly Ochieng, a Dakar-based analyst, says the economic incentives for attending the summit are much more limited because Moscow offers fewer large investment commitments than the United States or China.
Ochieng states that political incentives remain the primary reason why African countries attend the summit.
Sergey Eledinov, a former Russian officer and security analyst, warns that securing fragile governments may backfire because survival does not necessarily create loyalty.

uncertain.text: A separate attempt by Niger to sell existing uranium stockpiles remains in dispute.
Analysts caution that the appearance of Russian flags at African demonstrations does not indicate widespread or uniform public support.

terms.definition: Russia's state-owned nuclear energy corporation overseeing civil nuclear projects and uranium mining ventures.

removed.text: Human Rights Watch has accused Africa Corps forces in Mali of killing civilians and torturing detainees, though the full extent of abuses remains disputed or unresolved.
why: Evidence confirms the HRW accusations, but does not explicitly mention the extent of abuses being disputed.

explained.headline: El Salvador deploys more than 2,000 troops to Haiti

happened.text: El Salvador announced it will send more than 2,000 soldiers to Haiti to search for four missing aviation technicians and fight armed gangs.
The deployment follows the ambush and disappearance of four Salvadoran air force technicians who were travelling in an armoured vehicle in Croix-des-Bouquets.
Simultaneously, Haitian electoral authorities postponed the first round of presidential and parliamentary elections from December 13 to July 18, 2027.

background.text: Haiti has not held elections since 2016, and the political vacuum has deepened following the 2021 assassination of President Jovenel Moise.

matters.text: The ongoing violence disrupts farming and food deliveries, leading to severe hunger across the Caribbean country.
An international food security assessment projects that the number of people facing acute hunger will rise to 6.35 million by mid-2027.
The deployment of additional Salvadoran soldiers is intended to reinforce security operations and rescue efforts alongside Haitian authorities.

uncertain.text: It remains unclear whether the newly arrived Salvadoran troops will join the multinational Gang Suppression Force or operate separately.
No armed group has claimed responsibility for the disappearance of the four Salvadoran technicians.
The true identities and origins of four bodies handed over to special forces remain disputed after Salvadoran President Bukele stated they did not match the missing servicemen.

terms.definition: The official body responsible for organising and administering national and local elections.

removed.text: Nayib Bukele, El Salvador's president, has already sent troops and threatened to destroy Haiti's gangs if they do not release the missing personnel.
Armed gangs currently control much of the capital, Port-au-Prince, making voting preparations dangerous and voter registration difficult.
why: Evidence confirms gang control makes registration difficult but does not explicitly name the entire capital.
